item.title: The 1-week time tracking experiment
item.description:
A new newsletter deep dive makes the case for tracking your time for just one week — even if nobody requires you to. The piece lays out what to log, why the exercise is worth doing, and what to ask AI afterward to make sense of the results.

The appeal is the low commitment: a single week of logging is enough to reveal where the hours actually go, versus where you think they go, and the AI angle turns a raw log into usable insight — patterns, time sinks, and trade-offs you can act on. For anyone working from home and feeling busy but unsure what the busyness is made of, it's a small experiment with a potentially outsized payoff: a clearer picture of your week, and a few concrete changes worth making.
